newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Union deal is foundation for future profit - Sabena.
newsitem.headline: Union deal is foundation for future profit - Sabena.

text.p: Belgian airline Sabena said on Thursday a provisional deal with its main unions laid the foundation for a return to profit by 1998.
The company said the agreement, subject to approval by all staff, would cut costs by two billion francs as envisaged in its Horizon 98 profit restoration plan.

The deal includes adjustments in flexibility and working conditions until 1998 worth 750 million francs. Job cuts are to yield 820 million francs on an annual basis. A two-year wage freeze should cut costs by 430 million francs annually.
The measures constitute the unions' contribution to the Horizon 98 plan. Further cost cuts and revenue increases are to raise 2.7 billion francs.
Sabena chief executive officer Paul Reutlinger said four months of the talks with unions had sometimes been difficult, but always in a constructive spirit.
The deal was to safeguard the continuation and profitability of Sabena. "It allows us to focus our energy on satisfying our five million passengers," he said.
